title: A fixed boundary for zeta's zeros

paper.title: The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re(s) > 7/8

claim: The released proof excludes zeros of the Riemann zeta function to the right of 7/8, at every height. The full Riemann hypothesis remains open.

ai.contribution: Produced mathematical arguments and proof artifacts in OpenAI's research collection.
ai.human: OpenAI curated the release. Human assistance is acknowledged for the later, weaker 11/12 companion.
ai.disclosure: Zero-free-region work was an exception to the standard evaluation procedure; the full division of work is not disclosed.

evidence.label: Formal proof scope
evidence.text: The release lists a Lean formalization covering zeta, all Dirichlet L-functions, and a specified Hecke family. Later applications are excluded; this tracker has not rerun it.

comparison.before: Excluding zeros on the line Re(s) = 1 does not exclude a fixed band to its left.
comparison.after: A single boundary, 7/8, applies at every height.
comparison.conditions: The zero-free region is strictly Re(s) > 7/8; poles at 1 are excluded.
comparison.limit: This does not place all nontrivial zeros on 1/2, as the Riemann hypothesis requires.

title: When a quantum state has a compact description

paper.title: Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states

claim: The preprint claims that a specified class of lowest-energy quantum states on a square grid admits a polynomial-size tensor-network approximation of the entire state.

ai.contribution: Produced the manuscript within OpenAI's collection of model-generated research.
ai.human: OpenAI organized and published the evaluation; per-paper editing and checking roles are not itemized.
ai.disclosure: The repository's general process description is not a complete record of this paper's research process.

evidence.label: Released argument
evidence.text: Paper and source are available. The proof uses a companion area-law result; this tracker has not independently audited either argument.

evidence.label: Formalization availability
evidence.text: No PEPS entry was found in the release's formalization catalogue checked October 22, 2026.

comparison.before: An entanglement bound across each cut does not by itself supply one compatible approximation of the whole grid.
comparison.after: The claimed network has bond dimension at most C L^c and whole-vector error at most 1/L.
comparison.conditions: An open L × L grid; fixed local dimension, bounded nearest-neighbor interactions, a unique ground state, and a gap bounded below independently of L.
comparison.limit: It does not guarantee an efficient way to find the tensors or compute with them.

title: Can two fixed sets add up to the primes?

paper.title: The additive indecomposability of the primes

claim: The released theorem rules out two sets of nonnegative integers whose pairwise sums equal the primes apart from finitely many exceptions, when each set has at least two elements.

ai.contribution: Produced the mathematical manuscript and supporting proof artifacts, according to the release.
ai.human: OpenAI selected, organized and released the collection.
ai.disclosure: The model is unreleased; a detailed account of human intervention for this individual result is not supplied.

evidence.label: Formalization scope
evidence.text: OpenAI lists the full Ostmann theorem and its two-infinite-summands case; this tracker has not audited the Lean development.

comparison.before: Earlier work constrained what a hypothetical decomposition would have to look like.
comparison.after: The manuscript reports that every such decomposition is impossible, even after finitely many changes.
comparison.conditions: Both sets contain at least two nonnegative integers; every pairwise sum counts.
comparison.limit: This concerns the set of primes as a sumset. It does not settle Goldbach’s question about even numbers.

title: A stronger bound on compatible choices

ai.contribution: Helped derive key inequalities and proof ideas. Harmonic’s Aristotle assisted the later Lean formalization.
ai.human: Lee and Seo integrated the ideas, filled gaps, and independently rewrote some proofs.
ai.disclosure: The paper identifies contributions locally; it describes the two-color AI output as an incomplete proof sketch.

evidence.label: Research paper
evidence.text: The main theorem extends an equal-weight bound; a second theorem covers a two-color model.

evidence.label: Lean artifact

comparison.before: The cited bound used a common weight for all vertices.
comparison.after: Each vertex may have its own weight, while the lower bound still depends on the vertex degrees.
comparison.conditions: A finite simple graph; all weights are nonnegative.
comparison.limit: This bounds a weighted count. It is not an algorithm for finding the largest independent set.
